essay:
Technology in Education

In the modern time, technology is very important for the students. Many school are using computer and tablet in classroom. I think technology help students to learn more better, but also it have some problems.

First, technology make the learning more interesting. When teacher show a video about the science, students can see how the things is working. For example in my school we watched a video of volcano and everybody was very exciting. Also students can search informations on internet very fast, they dont need to go to library.

Second, technology is helping students who is shy. Some student dont like to speak in front of class but they can write there opinion in online forum. My friend Ravi was never talking in class, but in the online discussion he write very good ideas and teacher was suprised.

However technology have also disadvantage. Students can play games or watch videos instead of study. Sometime I also do this when I am suppose to do homework. Another problem is that not every families can buy a laptop, so some students cannot use it at home. This is not fair for them.

In conclusion, technology is good for education because it make learning interesting and help shy students. But schools must to control how students use it and also give devices to poor students. If we use technology in correct way, it can make education more better for everyone.

argument_structure.quote: I think technology help students to learn more better, but also it have some problems.
technology make the learning more interesting.
My friend Ravi was never talking in class, but in the online discussion he write very good ideas and teacher was suprised.
In conclusion, technology is good for education because it make learning interesting and help shy students.

criteria.summary: Frequent errors in agreement, articles, spelling and punctuation sometimes make meaning unclear.

strengths.quote: technology make the learning more interesting.
strengths.comment: You correctly use a simple subject‑verb structure, which shows you can build basic sentences.

strengths.quote: My friend Ravi was never talking in class, but in the online discussion he write very good ideas and teacher was suprised.
strengths.comment: You link ideas with ‘but’, showing awareness of coordination.

improvements.quote: technology help students to learn more better
improvements.issue: Incorrect verb form and comparative phrase; ‘help’ needs third‑person singular ‘helps’ and ‘more better’ is redundant.
improvements.suggestion: Change to ‘technology helps students learn better.’
improvements.example_rewrite: technology helps students learn better

improvements.quote: Many school are using computer and tablet in classroom.
improvements.issue: Subject‑verb agreement and article usage; ‘school’ should be plural and ‘computer’ needs an article.
improvements.suggestion: Write ‘Many schools are using computers and tablets in the classroom.’
improvements.example_rewrite: Many schools are using computers and tablets in the classroom.

improvements.quote: students can see how the things is working.
improvements.issue: Plural noun ‘things’ with singular verb ‘is’; also article missing before ‘things’.
improvements.suggestion: Use ‘how things work’ or ‘how the thing works.’
improvements.example_rewrite: students can see how things work.

improvements.issue: Wrong adjective; ‘exciting’ describes something that causes excitement, not a feeling. Use ‘excited’.
improvements.suggestion: Replace with ‘very excited.’
improvements.example_rewrite: everybody was very excited.

improvements.quote: they dont need to go to library.
improvements.issue: Missing apostrophe in contraction and missing article before ‘library’.
improvements.suggestion: Write ‘they don’t need to go to the library.’
improvements.example_rewrite: they don’t need to go to the library.

improvements.quote: technology is helping students who is shy.
improvements.issue: Relative clause verb agreement; ‘who is’ should be ‘who are’ because ‘students’ is plural.
improvements.suggestion: Change to ‘students who are shy.’
improvements.example_rewrite: technology is helping students who are shy.

improvements.issue: Spelling error ‘there’ should be ‘their’; also article ‘an’ needed before ‘opinion’.
improvements.suggestion: Write ‘they can write their opinion.’
improvements.example_rewrite: they can write their opinion.

improvements.issue: Spelling error ‘suprised’ → ‘surprised.’
improvements.suggestion: Correct the spelling.
improvements.example_rewrite: teacher was surprised.

improvements.issue: Verb agreement and article missing; ‘have’ → ‘has’ and ‘disadvantage’ needs ‘a’.
improvements.suggestion: Write ‘However, technology has also a disadvantage.’
improvements.example_rewrite: However, technology has also a disadvantage.

improvements.quote: Sometime I also do this when I am suppose to do homework.
improvements.issue: Adverb form ‘Sometime’ should be ‘Sometimes’; verb form ‘suppose’ should be ‘supposed’.
improvements.suggestion: Write ‘Sometimes I also do this when I am supposed to do homework.’
improvements.example_rewrite: Sometimes I also do this when I am supposed to do homework.

improvements.quote: but schools must to control how students use it
improvements.issue: Extra infinitive ‘to’; correct form is ‘must control’.
improvements.suggestion: Remove ‘to’: ‘but schools must control how students use it.’
improvements.example_rewrite: but schools must control how students use it.

improvements.quote: If we use technology in correct way, it can make education more better for everyone.
improvements.issue: Missing article before ‘correct way’ and redundant comparative ‘more better’.
improvements.suggestion: Write ‘in the correct way’ and ‘better’.
improvements.example_rewrite: If we use technology in the correct way, it can make education better for everyone.

criteria.summary: The essay has a recognizable introduction, body, and conclusion, but paragraph ordering and transitions are weak, causing ideas to jump.

strengths.quote: In the modern time, technology is very important for the students.
strengths.comment: You open with a clear introductory sentence that states the general topic.

strengths.quote: In conclusion, technology is good for education because it make learning interesting and help shy students.
strengths.comment: You provide a concluding sentence that restates your main point.

improvements.quote: First, technology make the learning more interesting. ... Second, technology is helping students who is shy.
improvements.issue: The body paragraphs are labeled ‘First’ and ‘Second’ but the counter‑argument appears later, breaking the logical flow.
improvements.suggestion: Arrange paragraphs as: (1) benefits, (2) drawbacks, (3) rebuttal/solution. Use transition words like ‘however’ to signal the shift.
improvements.example_rewrite: First, technology makes learning more interesting. However, it also has disadvantages.

improvements.issue: Missing clear topic sentence that signals the main claim of each paragraph.
improvements.suggestion: Begin each paragraph with a concise topic sentence that states the specific point you will discuss.
improvements.example_rewrite: Technology makes learning more interesting because it allows visual demonstrations.

improvements.issue: Abrupt jumps between ideas (e.g., from volcano video to searching information) without linking sentences.
improvements.suggestion: Add simple connective phrases such as ‘In addition,’ or ‘For example,’ to guide the reader.
improvements.example_rewrite: In addition, students can quickly search information on the internet.

criteria.summary: You state a clear position and give some supporting claims and evidence, but the support is often vague and the counter‑claim lacks a rebuttal.

strengths.quote: I think technology help students to learn more better, but also it have some problems.
strengths.comment: Your thesis identifies both a positive stance and acknowledges problems, giving a balanced position.

strengths.quote: My friend Ravi was never talking in class, but in the online discussion he write very good ideas and teacher was suprised.
strengths.comment: You provide a concrete example showing how technology helps shy students.

improvements.issue: The counter‑claim is mentioned but never explained with specific evidence.
improvements.suggestion: Add a concrete example (e.g., ‘students may spend class time playing games instead of studying.’) and explain why this weakens the overall benefit.
improvements.example_rewrite: However, technology also has disadvantages; for instance, some students use tablets to play games during class.

improvements.issue: No rebuttal that addresses the counter‑claim.
improvements.suggestion: Include a sentence that shows how the drawback can be managed (e.g., ‘Teachers can set usage limits to prevent gaming.’).
improvements.example_rewrite: Nevertheless, teachers can limit access to non‑educational sites, reducing this problem.

improvements.issue: Evidence is often vague (“students can search informations on internet very fast”).
improvements.suggestion: Provide specific data or a brief anecdote to make the claim stronger.
improvements.example_rewrite: Students can find reliable sources in seconds; for example, a recent study showed they locate research articles 40% faster using digital databases.

criteria.summary: The essay repeats common arguments about technology and uses several clichéd phrases; personal anecdotes are present but could be developed further.

strengths.quote: My friend Ravi was never talking in class, but in the online discussion he write very good ideas and teacher was suprised.
strengths.comment: Including a personal example about your friend adds a hint of your own voice.

strengths.quote: Sometime I also do this when I am suppose to do homework.
strengths.comment: You relate the topic to your own experience, which is a good step toward originality.

improvements.issue: Frequent reliance on generic statements like ‘technology is very important’ and ‘in modern time.’
improvements.suggestion: Replace generic phrasing with specific observations or unique perspectives (e.g., describe a particular app your school uses).
improvements.example_rewrite: Our school uses the ‘Kahoot!’ app, which turns quizzes into competitive games that keep students engaged.

improvements.issue: Use of filler clichés such as ‘more better’ and ‘in correct way.’
improvements.suggestion: Choose precise language; avoid redundant comparatives and vague modifiers.
improvements.example_rewrite: If we use technology correctly, it can improve education for everyone.

improvements.issue: Voice is inconsistent; sentences shift between formal and informal tones.
improvements.suggestion: Decide on a tone (e.g., academic) and maintain it throughout, using consistent verb forms and vocabulary.
improvements.example_rewrite: Technology enhances learning by providing visual resources and supporting shy students through online forums.

grammar_errors.quote: technology help students to learn more better
grammar_errors.explanation: Third‑person singular needs ‘s’ on the verb; comparative ‘more better’ is redundant.

grammar_errors.quote: Many school are using computer and tablet in classroom
grammar_errors.correction: Many schools are using computers and tablets in the classroom
grammar_errors.explanation: Plural nouns need plural verbs and articles; ‘computer’ and ‘tablet’ require articles and plural ‘s’.

grammar_errors.quote: students can see how the things is working
grammar_errors.correction: students can see how things work
grammar_errors.explanation: Plural noun ‘things’ must match plural verb ‘are’; the phrase can be simplified.
'Exciting' describes something that causes excitement; the correct adjective for feeling is 'excited'.

grammar_errors.quote: they dont need to go to library
grammar_errors.correction: they don’t need to go to the library
grammar_errors.explanation: Contractions need an apostrophe; singular count nouns need an article.

grammar_errors.quote: technology is helping students who is shy
grammar_errors.correction: technology is helping students who are shy
grammar_errors.explanation: Relative clause verb must agree with its antecedent ‘students’ (plural).
'There' is a location adverb; the possessive adjective is 'their'.

grammar_errors.correction: However, technology has also a disadvantage
grammar_errors.explanation: Singular subject needs ‘has’; an indefinite article is required before ‘disadvantage’.

grammar_errors.quote: Sometime I also do this when I am suppose to do homework
grammar_errors.correction: Sometimes I also do this when I am supposed to do homework
grammar_errors.explanation: 'Sometime' is an adverb meaning ‘once’; the correct adverb is ‘sometimes’. Past participle ‘supposed’ is needed after ‘am’.

grammar_errors.quote: but schools must to control how students use it
grammar_errors.correction: but schools must control how students use it
grammar_errors.explanation: Modal ‘must’ is followed directly by the base verb; the infinitive ‘to’ is unnecessary.

grammar_errors.quote: If we use technology in correct way, it can make education more better for everyone
grammar_errors.correction: If we use technology in the correct way, it can make education better for everyone
grammar_errors.explanation: Missing article ‘the’; comparative ‘more better’ is redundant; use ‘better’ alone.

feedback.overall_summary: Your essay shows a clear understanding of the topic and includes personal examples, which is a good start. However, frequent grammar mistakes and weak organization make it hard for readers to follow your argument. Focus on correcting basic sentence errors, improving paragraph transitions, and adding stronger evidence and a rebuttal to strengthen your position.
top_priorities: Fix recurring grammar errors (subject‑verb agreement, articles, verb forms).
Re‑organize paragraphs with clear topic sentences and logical order, adding transitions.
Develop a rebuttal to address the counter‑claim and provide more specific evidence.
top_strengths: You state a clear position that acknowledges both benefits and problems.
Personal anecdotes (Ravi, your own experience) give the essay a voice.
You include a concluding sentence that restates the main idea.
feedback.next_step_exercise: Write three short paragraphs (5‑6 sentences each) on a new topic. In each paragraph, start with a clear topic sentence, include one specific example, and end with a concluding sentence. Pay special attention to subject‑verb agreement and correct article usage.
